text: External primary weather feed degradation :: The primary weather vendor's feed became degraded/noisy during the window, emitting irregular or stale weather observations that propagated downstream. :: Root cause is likely external degradation of the primary weather source, with forecast-pipeline warnings as a downstream symptom.

Ingestion service introduced inconsistent weather observations :: Ingestion mishandled weather observations during the window, e.g. mixing primary and secondary vendor records, failing to deduplicate, or writing inconsistent timestamps. :: The variability was introduced at the ingestion boundary before forecast-pipeline read the data.

forecast-pipeline quality check misbehaving :: A recent code or configuration change caused the variability.weather_observations quality check to be too strict or to compute variance incorrectly over the current window. :: The warning may be self-generated by forecast-pipeline's quality-check logic.

postgres served inconsistent weather observation data :: Weather observation rows in postgres were partially written, stale, or had inconsistent timestamps/values during the window, causing spurious variability when read by forecast-pipeline. :: The common data store served inconsistent weather observations to the pipeline.

Secondary weather vendor failover instability :: The secondary weather vendor feed activated or flapped during failover and delivered observations with different cadence or calibration than the primary feed, creating a mixed-source series. :: Unstable weather-vendor failover produced the variability seen by forecast-pipeline.
